title: The 668-Horsepower Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing Is The Corvette For Non-Corvette Buyers - Top Speed
content: Walking by this baby blue Cadillac in a parking lot, you'd be forgiven for not knowing what's going on underneath the sheet metal. On startup, there's a hint. Its 6.2-liter V-8 is hardly muted. Toggle a few switches, and you can tame the roar a bit, quieting the exhaust in Tour mode. In that setting, despite the addition of an $18,000 precision package that greatly stiffens the suspension, you can indeed drive this Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing as a commuter, loafing to the grocery, fetching the kiddos, and enjoying the stellar, 16-speed AKG sound system. If you want a sports car, but two-seaters don't fit your lifestyle, spending $100,000 on this Cadillac is, dare I say it, a sane alternative. Oh, and yes, you'd be getting some Corvette-ness in the process — though that bears further explanation. The supercharged 6.2-liter LT4 V-8 making 668 horsepower under the hood of this Cadillac has seen duty in a Corvette — but in the prior-generation C7, not the new C8. No matter. Mash the throttle and your kidneys will be pushed deep into the Caddy's sport buckets, as the CT5-V Blackwing is capable of hitting 100 MPH in less than eight seconds. The experience is thrilling, and although my tester had a 10-speed manumatic, it shifts quickly either in automated mode or via a pair of paddles. You can quicken that gearbox and stiffen the chassis at the touch of a button. You're starting with the miracle of Magnetic Ride Control, where dampers adapt to bumps in milliseconds. That's a blessing, because even though the default ride is firm, it's not painful. Switch to Sport Mode for even less body motion, and the system also holds up-shifts longer and downshifts more quickly. If that's not ferocious enough, Track Mode bolts the Cadillac to the tarmac, shifts become ultra-quick, and throttle response is instant. If you're willing to spring for the CT5-V Blackwing, you're surely comparing it to the 717-horsepower, $123,300 BMW M5. If you can afford the Cadillac, perhaps you're not dissuaded by that considerable upcharge. With options, the CT5-V Blackwing can certainly cost as much or more; carbon-ceramic brakes alone will run you an extra $9,000. The CT5-V Blackwing has one major advantage over that BMW — it's considerably lighter, tipping the scales at just over 4,000 pounds. The M5 weighs 5,400 pounds. I've driven the wagon version of that BMW and it's pretty amazing. But the Cadillac is just quicker-witted. Its steering feels wired to your brain, and once the Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires are warm (thankfully the instrument cluster can tell you when they are), grip pulls above one g of cornering force. Grip loss is also predictable and progressive. And Cadillac engineered stability and traction control to allow just enough tail waggle to make the CT5-V entertaining, even below extreme velocity. Anyone considering the BMW will also compare the digs of this Detroit brawler to the amenities offered by that Bavarian machine. Of course, that comes down to taste—but also to how much that stuff matters to you. For instance, the same controllers that grace the steering wheel of this $100,000 Cadillac are the ones you'd find in Chevy's least-expensive offerings. These are familiar, handy, and logical. But from the turn signal stalk to the wiper control, there's just too much that reads as GM vanilla rather than what Cadillac is fighting for in BMW's Teutonic élan. Though Cadillac does get some of this right. You can opt to always see Track mode vitals, and this array prioritizes performance metrics over all else. Also, a 33-inch display wraps through the instrument cluster seamlessly across to the infotainment panel. Unlike with its EVs, GM includes CarPlay and Android Auto, and standalone climate buttons (rather than nesting these within a menu) let you stay focused on driving. I get why Cadillac offers $8,090 sport seats. Both BMW and Mercedes do at this tier, too. These are pretty comfortable for what they are, but I'd personally prefer a movable headrest and softer support. These buckets incorporate a massaging function, but you wouldn't have that need if the seat weren't quite so firm. This loaner also came with not one, but two carbon fiber accent packages totaling over $13,000. The front seat backs came caged in an armature of carbon fiber, and Cadillac frames the door lever pulls in enough carbon fiber to deploy as a rear wing on the CT5-V. Unfortunately, it all comes off as trying too hard rather than upscale. That said, I don't care. Personally, I'd just skip the extras since, performance-wise, the CT5-V Blackwing is at least as good as an M5. I like this manumatic. I'd even go so far as saying if I were buying the CT5-V Blackwing, I'd be tempted to go this route, because it's mighty forgiving when you're bopping through town, and it executes shifts beautifully, even when you're driving this car in anger. For me, the deciding factor between buying the six-speed manual gearbox and going with the automatic would be use case. If I had another car for daily driving (and anyone with $100,000 to spend very likely does) and didn't necessarily have to wrestle a third pedal in traffic all that often, I'd save the extra $3,675 Cadillac charges for the automatic and keep this car as close to stock as possible. Although, those carbon-ceramic brakes are superb. This car is special. It's fast, poised, and capable — and, sadly, production ends in December. Arguably, Cadillac's already proven that they know how to take a stock, $50,000 CT5 and massage it to near supercar standards. BMW does the same thing with the 5 Series. But Cadillac's sales have never come close to BMW or Mercedes sedan numbers. Cadillac says the CT5 will be back, and I hope so, especially because mainstream sedan sales (think Camry, Accord, etc.) are all rebounding in this country. Still, the leading American-branded sedan in this country is… the Tesla Model 3. Cadillac should fight for room here, and not just at $100,000. But also at that price point. Because you can't take your kids to soccer practice in a Corvette. But this Cadillac is perfect for that, and so much more. We want to hear from you. title: John V. Luca, Jr. Obituary Oct 31, 2026 - J. Bradley McGonigle Funeral Home and Crematory, Inc.

John V. Luca, Jr., 89, of West Middlesex, passed away on Saturday, October 31, 2026, in his home. Mr. Luca was born on November 5, 1936, in Sharon, a son of the late John and Maria Luca, Sr. He was a 1954 graduate of Farrell High School and served three years of active duty and seven years of reserves for the U.S. Army. Following his honorable discharge, he began working at Sharon Tube, retiring with 42 years of service. During his tenure, he worked as a crane operator and in the maintenance department. He was also active in the plant’s bowling league and Thursday Night Club. John was a member of Holy Cross Orthodox Church, Hermitage, where he was a member of the choir. He married his wife of 66 years, the former Darleen Toda, on June 12, 1960. They enjoyed traveling, visiting Florida for 40 years and Chautauqua Lake, NY, for 35 years. A man of many talents, John was an exceptional pool player and cook. He also enjoyed bowling, playing cards, going out to eat and doing the crossword puzzles in the newspaper. He is survived by his wife at home; a son, John V. Luca, III, and his wife, Paula, of West Middlesex; two granddaughters, Danielle (Patrick) Hughes, and Kylie Luca; and a great-grandson, Luca Hughes. In addition to his parents, John was preceded in death by a daughter, Jayne Marie Luca Farris; a brother, Valer Luca; and a half-brother, Paul. title: Munster v Sharks: Five takeaways as 'electric' youngster provides the 'stardust' in wet-weather horror show for hosts - Planet Rugby
content: Sharks full-back Zekethelo Siyaya was a bright spark against Munster. Following a 15-3 win for the Sharks over Munster in the United Rugby Championship (URC) on Saturday, here’s our five takeaways from Thomond Park. The Sharks came, saw and conquered in a thoroughly deserved triumph on the road, ending a perfect tour for JP Pietersen’s charges this month. Tries from Gianni Lombard and Ivan van Zyl plus a conversion and penalty from the former saw the South Africans seal four points in Limerick. In reply, all that Munster could muster was a JJ Hanrahan penalty a minute before the interval as they suffered a third defeat this URC campaign. Victory puts the Sharks in fourth position in the standings while Munster have slipped to 12th as the tournament goes into an international break. Remember the name, Zekhethelo Siyaya. This 19-year-old has been a breath of fresh air this season and was electric tonight in tough conditions. He cut through Munster’s line at will and went agonisingly close to scoring a worldie in the first period but for a non-bounce of the rugby ball. Bulls v Scarlets: Five takeaways as forgotten Springbok provides ‘cool head’ while ‘scary’ bench does its job Siyaya was voted Player of the Match by the watching supporters in a dominant poll, with his post-match interview showing that he is polite, calm and has a mature head on his shoulders as he learns from the senior players in the squad and also ex-Bok wing and current Sharks boss Pietersen. Victory at Cardiff and Munster is a hugely impressive return from the Sharks which comes on the back of an EPCR Challenge Cup win at Lyon. Pietersen and his coaching group are clearly doing wonderful things at the Durban outfit and what is most impressive is that they are getting positive performances even whilst missing the likes of Springboks Rugby World Cup winners Eben Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Makazole Mapimpi. Gone are the days of the under-performing Sharks it appears as there is a real drive throughout the entire squad to win every single battle on the rugby field this season and it’s translating into wins. They look a side connected that is well balanced and motoring very much in the right direction. Stormers v Ulster: Winners and losers as Springboks duo and ‘freak’ make it ‘Halloween nightmare’ for visitors The squad posed for a photograph on the field as they captured a special moment in their journey together. One senses there are more to come. On the flipside, what a horror start to the URC season for the men in red. Five games, one victory, one draw and now three losses on the board. The title glory under Graham Rowntree and top-of-the-table finish the following year must seem like a distant memory for their supporters. What has followed since those heady days has been nothing short of disastrous on and off the field and one worries 2026/27 could be painful. Want more from Planet Rugby? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for world-class coverage you can trust. That was how the Sharks won this clash in Limerick. Defensively they were formidable as they shut out Munster and forced errors with the wet ball, on attack their power and pace put them on the front foot and lastly their kicking game from Jaden Hendrikse and Lombard was also on point. It was a blueprint for wet weather rugby and with the stardust of Siyaya at full-back causing havoc, the result tonight never really felt in doubt. title: Northampton Saints v Gloucester: Five takeaways as Henry Pollock 'taken out of the firing line' - Planet Rugby
content: Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock in action for Northampton Saints. Following a 28-14 victory for Northampton Saints over Gloucester, here are our five takeaways from the Gallagher PREM encounter at Franklin’s Gardens on Saturday. Northampton and Gloucester both moved into the international break in the top-four, but it is the Saints who will enter this period much the happier after producing an excellent performance following the visitors’ fast start. The Cherry and Whites were much the better team early on, going 14-0 in front thanks to tries from Max Llewellyn and Will Joseph, but the hosts edged themselves back into the contest in a fashion which was quite unlike the Saints. Usually renowned for their free-flowing style, the East Midlands outfit managed to get on top up front and battered their way through the heart of Gloucester. Their forward excellence enabled them to level the scores at the break via Tom Pearson and Curtis Langdon before they controlled the second period. It took them a while to get the scores their dominance deserved but quick-fire efforts from George Hendy and Rory Hutchinson sealed the bonus-point win and took them into third, just behind Saturday’s opponents. Northampton and England were already without Fin Smith and it looks like he will be joined on the sidelines by his half-back partner Alex Mitchell, who limped off in the first period with a hamstring injury. They would have very much been favourites to start together against the Wallabies next weekend, which means Jack van Poortvliet and either Marcus Smith or George Ford will be in the hotseat at the start of the Nations Championship. Despite Van Poortvliet taking the reins for the July Tests, Mitchell remains the best scrum-half in the country and it will be a big blow should the 29-year-old be unavailable for the Australia. What will make it more concerning for the Red Rose is that his understudy, Archie McParland, was absent from this encounter through injury. Some in Northampton would say that he has been playing even better than Mitchell. He is very much in the mould of the elder statesman with his ability to raise the tempo and snipe around the fringes but he picked up an issue during the week. However, the Saints could also call on another fine young scrum-half in Jonny Weimann, who was outstanding when the starting nine exited the game. While the Mitchell news will dominate matters, there was plenty to like about some of the prospective England players. Charlie Atkinson was the beneficiary of Smith’s injury and he showed a number of classy touches, continuing his fine form at the start of this season. Outside of him at 12 was Seb Atkinson, who wasn’t actually named in the 36-man training squad due to a minor injury but will surely be involved when the updated group is revealed ahead of the Wallabies Test. He was a physical presence on both sides of the ball and his pass for Joseph’s try was delightful. The finish from Joseph was just as sublime as he wriggled his way through a couple of defenders to touch down. The way he contorted his body was akin to his older brother, Joseph, who had an exceptional Test career, and it will not be surprised if Will follows suit. As for the Saints, Pearson, who has been recalled to the England squad, and Alex Coles were among their standouts up front, while Tommy Freeman had some excellent surges at outside centre, but Steve Borthwick will simply be pleased that mostly everyone appeared to get through the clash unscathed. Bath v Sale Sharks: Five takeaways as Finn Russell has ‘first and last laugh’ over George Ford but ‘oh-so-classy’ player the star of the show The consensus from observes would be that Gloucester have had an excellent start to the season and the defending champions have endured a mixed opening to the campaign but, ahead of the international break, their respective records both read three wins and two defeats with them both on 16 points. Gloucester remain in front due to points difference but Northampton showed that, while Phil Dowson’s men are perhaps not quite at their best at the moment, they can still raised their game when it matters, ride the momentum and eke out big victories. It is a skill the Cherry and Whites have yet to truly master after failing to take advantage of good starts against Leicester Tigers and Northampton to succumb to the East Midlands duo. It is certainly no disgrace to lose to those sides, but on both occasions, the Tigers and Saints turned the screw and they did not have a response. It got to the hour mark and we wondered where Henry Pollock was. However, after last weekend’s antics, perhaps Dowson thought it was best to take him out of the spotlight. It helped that the player he eventually replaced, Pearson, was having a mightily fine game with his sheer physicality helping them to win the gain line battle in the second period, deservedly earning him the player of the match award. When Pollock did finally enter the fray on 67 minutes, the 21-year-old was on his best behaviour as he stayed away from the type shenanigans we saw at Welford Road. There was the odd spark, including a try-saving hit – albeit it came after he had missed the initial tackle – and a weaving run with the clock in the red, but it felt like a case of the Saints of trying to take him out of the headlines, for this week at least. It does raise the question of what Borthwick does next week, though. In truth, he hasn’t had the best start to the season and the England boss will want to avoid the type of Welford Road mischief which could provide added motivation to the Aussies, just as it did Leicester. Pollock should still be in the 23, but his Test chances haven’t been helped over recent weeks. title: 4 Compact SUVs With Better Ratings Than The Honda CR-V - SlashGear
content: While Ford's F-150 Series is the bestselling vehicle in the U.S., when it comes to type of vehicle, Americans buy more compact SUVs than any other, including pickup trucks and midsize SUVs. Smaller SUVs give buyers the best of both worlds — they handle more like a car than a truck, but they offer more passenger and cargo space than your typical sedan. They also give drivers a bit of height and extra ground clearance. Additionally, they are easier to park than full-size SUVs and other larger vehicles, and easier to maneuver on tight city streets and small parking lots. Many compact SUVs offer excellent safety ratings and come standard with the same safety features that you find in larger vehicles. They're also an affordable option, with many starting well under $35,000. The 2026 Honda CR-V was named Kelley Blue Book's top compact SUV. It's the automaker's bestselling vehicle, offering an easy ride, a nice lineup of standard tech and safety features, and an attractive starting price. Kelley Blue Book isn't the only authority in the game, however. There are plenty of several other trusted reviewers, including U.S. News and World Report and Consumer Reports. Here are four compact SUVs that come out on top in other evaluations. The Toyota RAV4 has been a mainstay on the road since the mid-1990s. Now in its sixth generation, the 2026 model starts at $31,900, which is just a few hundred more than the 2027 Honda CR-V. The Toyota is one of Consumer Reports' top-ranking compact SUVs, putting it higher than the CR-V, and it also earned the Consumer Reports Recommended Model badge, which recognizes vehicles that earned a good Overall Score. It takes into account reliability, road test results, owner satisfaction, and more. All models of the 2026 RAV4 have a hybrid powertrain with a 2.5-Liter Dynamic Force 4-cylinder engine. There is no traditional gas-powered option available, but this means that no matter which trim you select, you can expect excellent gas mileage. The base LE model with front-wheel drive sees a combined 43 mpg, while other models see anywhere from 38 mpg to 43 mpg. The cabin seats five and comes standard with a 10.5-inch infotainment touch screen and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. It received mostly "Good" ratings from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS), though it was not named a Top Safety PIck due to its rating of "Acceptable" in the Moderate Overlap Front category. Overall, Toyota offers the RAV4 in six trims, with the top-tier Limited model currently priced at $43,300. The RAV4 is covered by a three-year, 36,000 mile basic warranty and an eight-year, 100,000 mile hybrid system warranty. The 2026 Hyundai Tucson ranks at the top of U.S. News & World Report's compact SUV rankings, and Consumer Reports also places the Tucson above the CR-V in its ratings. It's also less expensive than both the CR-V and the RAV4. The base SE model starts at $29,700, and all trims have the same 2.5-liter 4-cylinder engine putting out 187 horsepower. Front-wheel drive is standard, and all-wheel drive is available on all models. If you select all-wheel drive, you can expect to see a combined 26 mpg, while front-wheel drive models see 28 mpg. U.S. News & World Report gave the Tucson high marks for its roomy cabin, which includes seating for five and above-average cargo space, along with its long list of standard safety and driver assistance features. It was also the winner of the U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best Compact SUV for the Money award and the 2026 Best Compact SUV for Families award. Additionally, it earned the Consumer Reports Recommended badge. Standard features include a 12.3-inch touch screen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, forward collision-avoidance assist, a driver attention warning, rear cross-traffic collision-avoidance assist, smart cruise control, and a 6-way adjustable driver's seat. The Tucson is also available in hybrid and plug-in hybrid options. The 2026 Subaru Forester is another compact SUV that starts under $30,000. Both the gasoline and hybrid models are ranked higher than the CR-V by Consumer Reports, and it comes standard with all-wheel drive. Neither option is particularly fast off the mark, but drivers can expect good fuel economy from models with a traditional powertrain, and excellent fuel economy from hybrid models. Buyers will pay a bit more for Forester Hybrid, which has an MSRP of $34,730, but it has a range of up to 581 miles and a combined 35 mpg. Both the hybrid Forester and the traditional Forester are Consumer Reports Recommended vehicles. All models have the same 2.5-liter Boxer 4-cylinder engine, whether buyers opt for a hybrid or traditional powertrain. All trims save the base model come with an 11.6-inch infotainment screen. If you love to go off-roading but don't want to give up that Subaru safety and durability, the automaker offers the Wilderness trim. It has a higher 9.3-inch ground clearance, a front-view monitor, all-terrain tires, and an X-MODE that is designed to complement the symmetrical all-wheel drive with Snow/Dirt and Deep Snow/Mud modes. The Forester was named a Top Safety Pick+ by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). Subaru provides a three-year, 36,000-mile limited warranty and a five-year, 60,000-mile powertrain warranty. Hybrid components have an eight-year, 100,000-mile warranty. Cars.com doesn't name the popular RAV4 or the CR-V as its number one choice for compact SUVs. Instead, the 2026 Volkswagen Tiguan takes the top spot, but there's a catch. The automotive marketplace and reviewer specifically cites the SEL R-Line Turbo trim, which is the top-tier Tiguan model. This compact SUV has a base price of $31,205 for the 2027 S trim, but the SEL R-Line Turbo starts at just over $43,000. The 2027 Tiguan is available now, but is very similar to the 2026 model year, which introduced a complete redesign. Cars.com calls the high-end trim "without question, the nicest vehicle here for the money" when comparing the Tiguan to the CR-V, the Tucson Hybrid, the RAV4, and other compact SUVs. It was also impressed with the TIguan's performance and high-end feel. The SEL R-Line Turbo offers luxurious amenities such as heated seats with a massage function, ambient lighting, a heated steering wheel, and a 15-inch touchscreen. The 2027 SEL R-Line Turbo has a more powerful variant of the same turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine that's in lower trims, but it produces 268 horsepower compared to 201 horsepower in less expensive models. All-wheel drive is standard, and buyers will also appreciate the head-up display, hands-free power liftgate, and three-zone automatic climate control. Volkswagen offers a four-year, 50,000-mile standard warranty.

title: Karma Turns the Revero Into the Wild Eximius 1, a One-Off Hybrid Packing a 6.2-Liter V-8 - Car and Driver
content: The track-ready sedan can zip to 60 mph in 2.7 seconds and wears aggressive aerodynamics and carbon-fiber bodywork. Personalization is the latest trend to sweep the automotive world, with nearly every high-end automaker launching a specific division that caters to the needs of its wealthiest customers. Porsche has Sonderwunsch, Bugatti has Sur Mesure, and Rolls-Royce has its Coachbuild program. Now Karma Automotive, a small American brand known for slinky plug-in hybrid sedans, is launching its own program called Eximius, and has revealed its first one-off, the Eximius 1, at the Concours at Wynn in Las Vegas. Karma Automotive, if you aren’t familiar, was birthed from the ashes of Fisker Automotive, and has sold an evolution of the Fisker Karma, known as the Revero and GS-6, on and off for most of the past decade. The Revero is a series hybrid, with a turbocharged three-cylinder serving as a generator to charge a battery that feeds electricity to a pair of rear-mounted electric motors. Although the Revero is being replaced by the new Gyesera, which further hones the same design and powertrain philosophy, this year, Karma is making sure the Revero goes out with a bang with this new one-off. The Eximius 1 takes the Revero platform and turns it up to eleven. This special one-off trades the three-cylinder for a far more compelling engine. Under the hood lies a 6.2-liter V-8, and the plug-in series hybrid powertrain produces a total of 1195 horsepower, which is well over 600 hp more than you get in the Revero. Karma claims the Eximius 1 can rocket to 60 mph in 2.7 seconds and can hit a top speed of 200 mph. Given the Eximius 1’s more extreme performance, Karma has fitted it with carbon-ceramic, two-piece slotted brake rotors and Öhlins semi-active dampers. The Eximius 1 is nearly two inches wider than a standard Revero, and carbon-fiber is used extensively throughout the car. Look closely at the bodywork, and you’ll be able to spot exposed carbon-fiber on the front fenders, with the blue paint fading in gradually over the carbon weave on the front doors, a truly unique finish. The Eximius 1 rides on 21-inch magnesium center-lock wheels. Designed for driving on the track, the Eximius 1 sports a fittingly dramatic aerodynamic package. Up front, there’s a carbon front splitter, sandwiched by gaping air intakes that integrate an LED line, which, when viewed with the LED element in the headlights, creates an arrow shape pointing toward the center of the car. Two thin nostrils sit next to the headlights, giving the car a sinister sneer. Vents have been carved into the front fenders to release air pressure from the wheel wells, and a large panel emblazoned with the number 5 incorporates a vent to extract hot air from the brakes. Below, a billet aluminum exhaust tip hints at the Eximius 1’s performance capabilities. An additional fin sits proud of the bodywork near the rear doors, and the rear end features a massive diffuser and a towering wing. Inside, Karma has fitted blue-tinted carbon-fiber to the seats, steering wheel, center console, doors, and dashboard. The Recaro bucket seats are padded in blue Alcantara and blue leather on the bottom and Alcantara in a hue called Moondust up top. The accelerator, brake pedal, and dead pedal have been crafted from billet machined aluminum, and Karma simplified the center console to only include the necessary controls, including a red emergency kill switch. The Eximius program will allow Karma’s customers to request modifications to the body, powertrain, and other performance components of the vehicle. Karma says it will create a maximum of nine bespoke vehicles based on each series production model that it launches. The Eximius 1 is the first, and it will be delivered to its owner in 2027. title: Virgil van Dijk: What a fixture this is - Liverpool v Arsenal is always special - Liverpool FC
content: “What a fixture,” Virgil van Dijk says of Liverpool’s Premier League showdown with Arsenal on Sunday. A run of four consecutive Anfield outings for the Reds concludes with a visit by the reigning champions. Andoni Iraola’s team enter the game against the Gunners having been victorious in each of their last five matches across all competitions. In his matchday programme notes, Van Dijk underscores what will be necessary if they are to enhance that streak to six and details his anticipation for a mouthwatering encounter. “It is rare to have four successive games at home, but what a fixture we have to round off that series,” writes the captain. “Games against Arsenal are always special, and Sunday’s will be no different. I know that you guys will be up for it, and we will be too. These are the games everybody wants to be involved in, so let’s give it everything and look to continue our positive run of form. “It was important that we progressed in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night. Chelsea, as we expected, gave us a really tough game, but I thought we stood up to the task as a team really well, and we got our rewards in the penalty shootout. Highlights: Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea | Reds win on penalties! “Now we have another home draw, and another tough game against Bournemouth ahead of us, but that is for another day. Our focus now turns to the Premier League, to Arsenal, and we have to be ready for the big challenge that they will pose. “They have shown over a number of seasons what a strong team they are, and if we want to come away with all three points then we will need to be at, or at least very close to, our best. “That starts, as usual, with our attitude and our work ethic. You don’t get easy, comfortable afternoons in the Premier League, and you certainly don’t get them against Arsenal. “You have to be switched on from the first second, you have to be prepared to run hard, fight for everything and help your teammates out, with and without the ball, for 90 minutes-plus. “We have shown in recent weeks that we understand those challenges and that we are able to keep our heads and stick together, even when things don’t go our way in games. “There will be times, I’m sure, when we have to suffer without the ball, but it is important that we keep our composure and make sure that when we have the ball we show our own quality. “It is important too that we use the energy that you guys provide to push us forward. When Anfield is at its best, we are at our best, and vice versa. “Like I say, these are the games we relish, the ones we look forward to as players. Hopefully, we can give you all something big to celebrate.” Get your copy of the matchday programme at Anfield or order online here

title: Chelsea v Man Utd player ratings: Rogers and Palmer make the difference - how did Martinez rate? - BBC
content: Morgan Rogers took his Chelsea goals tally to six this season, but Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez was sent off Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer scored second-half goals as Chelsea secured a 2-0 home win over 10-man Manchester United, who endured another desperate day. Chelsea's record £117m signing Rogers opened the scoring in the 50th minute before United defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off after conceding a penalty, which Palmer converted. Here's how BBC Sport's reporters at Stamford Bridge rated the players and your verdicts on the performances. Chelsea beat 10-man Man Utd to heap further pressure on Carrick Mike Penders: The Belgian goalkeeper remains under pressure after his mistake against Tottenham last week, but he was steady here and made several comfortable saves. 7 Josh Acheampong: The young defender looked shaky early on but recovered well, making a fantastic block from a Bruno Fernandes volley and improving as the game went on. 6 Wesley Fofana: The Frenchman made a brilliant block from one of Amad Diallo's shots but was twice at fault as the winger broke clear on the counter-attack. His header also struck the post after taking a deflection off Moises Caicedo in a chaotic display. Fofana also won the second-half penalty. 5 Levi Colwill: The England defender was part of an overall poor defensive display but did not make any obvious errors himself. 6 Marco Palestra: The Italian made some good recovery runs on his first start for Chelsea but was also part of a below-par defensive display from an organisational perspective. 7 Moises Caicedo: Influential presence in a scrappy midfield battle, helping Chelsea compete physically in the centre of the pitch. 6 Romeo Lavia: Often the player who helped Chelsea play through United's pressure, sparking several counter-attacks with intelligent passing. Won the ball for Chelsea's opener. 7 Pedro Neto: Arguably Chelsea's most dangerous attacker but finishing let him down, with one effort saved and another fired well wide in the first half. 6 Cole Palmer: A quiet game by his standards and unconvincingly scored a second-half penalty. Aside from that, he attempted an ambitious effort from inside his own half and gifted United one of their major chances. 6 Estevao Willian: Lost possession with his first touch but recovered impressively. Looked lively throughout, having a couple of dangerous-looking shots on goal and two that he scored but were ruled out for offside. His set-pieces were also of consistent high quality. 8 Morgan Rogers: A surprisingly anonymous start and struggled in the number nine position until he was given the chance to run at United's defence, scoring with a sublime dink in the 50th minute. 8 Pep Chavarria (on 71, Palestra): Game was already won when he entered. 6 Senne Lammens: Alive to Palmer's attempt to catch him out with a quickly taken free-kick. Was lucky to get away with a poor save early on, thanks to offside flag. Solid after that. No chance with Rogers goal. 7 Leny Yoro: Speed essential to deal with Chelsea counter-attacks but sometimes ran out of position. 7 Harry Maguire: Authoritative presence at heart of defence for most part but yet again unable to stop gap opening up for Rogers to score. 7 Lisandro Martinez: Did OK and looked good - until Chelsea scored. Then gave penalty away and red-carded for ridiculous moment of recklessness. 3 Diogo Dalot: Played out of position again at left-back and Estevao threatened down his side, but Dalot stuck to his task gamely. 6 Andrey Santos: So close to a memorable goal against his old club. Crucial intervention to deny Moises Caicedo a clear sight at goal at the other end. Difficult second half. 5 Carlos Baleba: Was having his best game in a United shirt so far and tried to prod the visitors forward. But impetuous tackle in midfield proved extremely costly as Rogers ran through to score. 5 Amad Diallo: Looked sharp. Tested Mike Penders from long range and also at his near post. Fofana blocked another goal-bound effort. Should have scored before half-time. 7 Bruno Fernandes: Returned as captain and should have put the visitors ahead when Mbeumo picked him out. Nearly set up Mbeumo. Better but not brilliant. 6 Matheus Cunha: Most impact of any recent game. Linked well with the visitors' attack but didn't threaten a goal. 6 Bryan Mbeumo: Set up a chance for Fernandes, then nearly reached a far-post cross from his captain. Gave Chelsea a problem but couldn't get last bit right. 6 Kobbie Mainoo (on 58, Baleba): Not on long enough to make an impact before Martinez red. After that it was damage limitation. 6 Ayden Heaven (on 66, Andrey Santos): Time for a regular start? 5 Mason Mount (on 66, Cunha): Usual abuse from the home fans and nothing to answer it with. 5 After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Team news - Liverpool FC
content: Read the latest team news updates from both camps ahead of Liverpool’s Premier League clash with Arsenal on Sunday. Victor Munoz and Dominik Szoboszlai ‘have a chance’ to feature for the Reds in the 4.30pm GMT kick-off at Anfield. The pair last appeared at Brentford a fortnight ago, where they sustained minor injuries. Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola revealed it is possible they could return for the visit of the reigning champions. “They have a chance. But I don’t know for sure if they will be involved or not. We still have two days so I think we have a chance, yes.” The Reds will be aiming to chalk up a sixth consecutive victory across all competitions and a third in a row in the Premier League. This meeting with the Gunners is match seven of nine fixtures in a 28-day spell between international breaks for Iraola’s charges. The boss made seven changes to his starting XI in midweek as Liverpool drew 1-1 with Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and won 6-5 on penalties. Press Conference: Liverpool vs Arsenal | Andoni Iraola “You have to do a lot of the job with the analysts, in the video room, with the board – without spending the legs,” he said. “But I think our players are very used to it, so a lot of the work is done and now it’s more a matter of getting the decisions right in terms of the loading, freshening the legs. “We are changing a lot from game to game and I think we will continue this approach, because I think it’s going well.” Jeremie Frimpong is currently sidelined with a muscle injury, and Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni are long-term absentees. Training photos: Liverpool's preparations on Friday Arsenal, meanwhile, are checking on the condition of Noni Madueke, who was not involved in their tie at Fleetwood Town on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta told the media on Friday: “We don’t know yet, we’ll have a training session tomorrow. “[We’ll] see if he can complete that full session tomorrow and as I said, I will know whether he’s available or not.” Bukayo Saka has been out of action since suffering an issue in the Gunners’ Champions League fixture at Bayern Munich earlier this month. “We want to have him as quick as possible,” said Arteta. “The player is desperate, he’s feeling much better than he was a few days ago. “He looks like [he could return before the next international break]; we need to wait and see how he evolves.” Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice and Christos Tzolis are all in training and on course to be available for the Anfield encounter, Arteta confirmed. Max Dowman is beginning a three-match suspension after being sent off against Fleetwood. Fleetwood Town 1-1 (5-3 pens) Arsenal (October 27): Meslier, Hincapie, Salmon, Mosquera, Timber, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Havertz, Dowman, O’Neill, Gyokeres.

title: Premier League today: How to watch Chelsea v Manchester United, TV channels & live stream Saturday 31 October - The Guardian
content: How will Chelsea and Manchester United fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options Chelsea and Manchester United both need a response to recent bad results. The former suffered a penalty shootout Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool on Wednesday days after a dismal home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League. The latter, meanwhile, have endured a chaotic week despite not playing a match. Michael Carrick is still in place as United manager despite widespread belief that Sunday’s 3-0 loss to Bournemouth would be his final act. Saturday’s meeting at Stamford Bridge could be pivotal for both Xabi Alonso and Carrick. Chelsea and Manchester United aren’t where they want to be and this encounter will give a sense of their chances of changing that. Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s Premier League fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options. Without João Pedro, Chelsea have struggled for attacking fluency in their last two games. Alonso has used Morgan Rogers and Emmanuel Emegha as deputy No 9s without success, which could point to Danny Welbeck starting against his former club on Saturday. Manchester United are similarly struggling for attacking fluency, as well as defensive solidity, midfield control and a general sense of a dressing room fighting for their manager. What was widely expected to be the first match of the post-Carrick era is now another chance for the 45-year-old to turn things around. United are winless in their last eight matches in all competitions while Chelsea have kept just one clean sheet in eight Premier League outings. All points to this match being a volatile one that could swing either way. Player to watch: Morgan Rogers, Chelsea – Perhaps lucky not to be sent off against Tottenham Hotspur, Rogers has registered five goal contributions in just eight league games for Chelsea.
